title: Orchestration roadmap sync — prep + action items
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional orchestration / roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Target sync: 2026-05-22 11:00am PT (30m) — quick, focused

Attendees (invite list):
- Leah Park (me) — product (roadmap lead)
- Camila Ortega — applied ML (model rollout + evals)
- Ben Zhang — serving runtime (latency/cost)
- Marcus Li — infra / dedicated capacity
- Priya Rao — product (release PM)

Goal: align on prioritization and rollout approach for Q3 effort to improve inference economics (batching + caching + quantization profiles) and confirm owners, canary plan, and metrics to gate release.

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick context (2m) — what problem we solve (cost + p99 spikes)
2) Proposed deliverables for Q3 (5m) — scope: batching config UI, KV/prefix caching opt-in, quant profiles for 13B/70B family
3) Canary/rollout strategy options (8m) — canary by customer tier vs region vs model variant
4) Metrics and guardrails (7m) — what counts as success / rollback triggers
5) Decisions & owners (8m) — agree next steps, blockers, immediate asks

Notes / prep items (things I need before the meeting):
- Get baseline numbers from Ben: current p50/p95/p99 latency per model family for hosted vs dedicated (last 7d rolling) and cost-per-1k-tokens estimates. (Ben: RT-2345 ticket probably has partial data)
- Camila: short eval plan to validate output quality after 4-bit quant profile for Mistral-derived 13B (10 prompt set). Bring quick pass/fail thresholds.
- Marcus: host capacity constraints table (reserved vs burst) and whether we can reserve a small pool for canary traffic.
- Priya: product-side prioritization constraints (customers on dedicated vs hosted, enterprise SLAs) — who to notify for canary.

Open questions to surface in sync (put on board if we don't answer):
- Can we auto-fallback to a known-compatible model variant if quantized path fails accuracy checks? impact on latency?
- How many customers (by % traffic) should be acceptable for an initial canary to get statistically meaningful telemetry?
- Do we need a separate billing flag for canary traffic if cost changes materially?

Quick draft of decision options (for vote):
A) Canary by customer tier: 1% enterprise + 2% PLG (random) — less operational overhead but risk to SLAs.
B) Canary by model variant: route a small % of traffic to quantized variant for non-SLA customers only.
C) Region-first canary: spin up in us-west-2 only, ramp by traffic weight.
(Recommend B + C combined: model-variant for non-SLA, region-limited.)

Metrics / guardrails to collect and alert on (must have before wider rollout):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 (same request distribution) and 95th of generation time per token
- Error rates: model runtime errors, malformed outputs, soft-fail fallback triggers
- Quality deltas: automated eval pass rate on small holdout (Camila to run) — threshold: <=2% degraded on key prompts otherwise rollback
- Cost delta: cost per 1k tokens measured from infra telemetry (Ben)
- User-visible regressions: any support tickets flagged by priority customers (Priya to notify)

Action items (owner — due)
- Ben: export p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k by model (13B, 70B families) for last 7d; attach to RT-2345 — due 2026-05-21 EOD
- Camila: run quick eval (100 prompt suite) comparing baseline -> quant-4bit for 13B; summarize fail modes and pass rate; put results in Confluence page — due 2026-05-21 noon
- Marcus: confirm whether we can reserve a 2-GPU pool for canary in us-west-2 and cost implication; note any infra config changes — due 2026-05-22 4pm PT
- Priya: prepare customer notification template and list of non-SLA customers to include (for canary selection) — due 2026-05-23
- Leah (me): draft rollout RFC with recommended option (B+C), include rollback conditions and dashboard list; share with group for review — initial draft 2026-05-24

Parking lot / follow-up (post-sync):
- Decide on telemetry retention window for canary metrics (how long before we decide to ramp)
- Legal / compliance check for running quantized models on enterprise datasets (Priya to loop in security if needed)
- Consider a beta channel that exposes toggles in Console (longer term)

Risks & mitigations (short notes):
- Risk: quantization introduces subtle quality regression. Mitigation: holdout eval set + canary traffic limited to non-SLA customers + auto-fallback policy to fall back to full-precision model on failure
- Risk: increased token cost upstream due to retries on fallback. Mitigation: simulate end-to-end cost with Ben + Marcus before ramping

Prep checklist for meeting (my personal):
- [ ] Pull RT-2345 notes and link specific charts (latency by model)
- [ ] Add Ben's exported CSV to drive and reference in meeting doc
- [ ] Draft recommended RFC skeleton (short) — will send at end of sync
- [ ] Slack ping Camila + Ben 30m before meeting to ensure they can share screens

Notes-to-self (tone: scratchpad):
- Keep it tight. Avoid design-deep dive. Need decisions: owner assignments and canary approach.
- If Camila flags >2% degrade, fallback to conservative: run more evals, do not ramp.
- Follow up: convert action items into RT tickets and assign in Monday planning.

End of scratchpad.
